intro: Listen to an announcement in a chemistry class.
text: Before we start today's lab, a quick safety reminder. Starting this week, the department is requiring splash goggles, not regular safety glasses, whenever acids are on the bench. If you don't have a pair, the stockroom will lend you one, but you'll need to leave your student ID there until you return it. Also, please tie back long hair and keep your bags in the cubbies by the door, not under the benches.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To introduce a new experiment involving acids
To explain new safety requirements for the lab
To announce that the stockroom will close early
To ask students to buy their own lab equipment
questions.explanation: The professor describes the new goggle rule and other safety expectations for the lab.

questions.prompt: According to the professor, what must students do to borrow goggles?
options: Pay a small rental fee at the stockroom
Ask the professor for written permission
Return them before the end of the day
Leave their student ID at the stockroom
questions.explanation: She says the stockroom will lend goggles if students leave their student ID until they return them.

intro: Listen to an announcement in a geology class.
text: Okay, about Saturday's field trip to Miller Canyon. The bus will now leave at seven thirty instead of eight, because the park asked us to finish before the afternoon heat. Meet in the parking lot behind the science building, not out front. Bring water, a hat, and sturdy shoes; sandals won't be allowed on the trail. And don't forget your field notebook, because you'll be sketching rock layers for your next assignment.

questions.prompt: Why was the departure time changed?
options: The bus company had a scheduling conflict.
The trail is longer than originally planned.
Some students have classes on Saturday afternoon.
The park wants the group to avoid the afternoon heat.
questions.explanation: The professor says the park asked the group to finish before the afternoon heat.

questions.prompt: What will students use their field notebooks for?
options: Recording the names of plants on the trail
Writing down directions to the canyon
Sketching rock layers for an assignment
Taking notes during a park ranger's talk
questions.explanation: He reminds students they will be sketching rock layers for their next assignment.

intro: Listen to an announcement in a history class.
text: I have an update about the midterm. Because so many of you asked for more time, the exam will now take place during our two-hour Thursday session instead of Tuesday. The format is also changing slightly: there will be three short-answer questions instead of five, plus one essay. I'll post a list of possible essay topics online by Friday, so you can prepare in advance. Your study guides from last week are still useful.

questions.prompt: What is the professor mainly announcing?
options: Changes to the timing and format of an exam
A new requirement for a research essay
The results of a recent midterm exam
The cancellation of a Thursday class
questions.explanation: She explains that the midterm is moving to Thursday and will have a different set of questions.

questions.prompt: Why was the exam moved to Thursday?
options: The professor will be away on Tuesday.
The classroom is unavailable on Tuesday.
The essay topics are not ready yet.
Students requested more time to complete it.
questions.explanation: The professor says the change was made because many students asked for more time.

intro: Listen to an announcement in a business class.
text: Hi everyone, I'm going over the rules for the group project. Teams should have four members, no more and no fewer. You can choose your own teammates, but please send me your team list by next Wednesday. If you haven't joined a team by then, I'll assign you to one. At the end of the project, each person will rate their teammates' contributions, and those ratings will count for ten percent of your grade.

questions.prompt: What will happen to students who are not on a team by next Wednesday?
options: The teaching assistant will place them on a team.
They will have to complete the project alone.
They will lose ten percent of their grade.
They will be allowed to form a team of two.
questions.explanation: He says that he will assign anyone without a team to one.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about the teammate ratings?
options: They will be shared with the whole class.
They must be submitted by next Wednesday.
They are optional for most of the students.
They will affect part of each student's grade.
questions.explanation: He states that the ratings will count for ten percent of the grade.

intro: Listen to an announcement in a biology class.
text: Next Monday we'll have a guest speaker, Dr. Ellen Park, a wildlife veterinarian who works at a rehabilitation center for injured birds. She'll talk about how the center treats birds and prepares them to return to the wild. Since she's coming in person, please read the short article I posted before class, and come with at least one question for her. The talk will start right at ten, so don't be late.

questions.prompt: Who is the guest speaker?
options: A researcher who studies bird migration
A zookeeper who trains birds for shows
A veterinarian who treats injured wild birds
A professor who writes about bird behavior
questions.explanation: The professor introduces Dr. Park as a wildlife veterinarian at a rehabilitation center for injured birds.

questions.prompt: What does the professor ask students to do before the talk?
options: Visit the bird rehabilitation center
Write a short summary of a lecture
Read an article and prepare a question
Sign up to introduce the speaker
questions.explanation: She asks students to read the posted article and bring at least one question.

intro: Listen to an announcement in an art history class.
text: For your next paper, you'll need to visit the university art museum and choose one painting from the landscape gallery on the second floor. The museum is free for students, but it's closed on Mondays, so plan accordingly. Photography is allowed, but no flash. Take careful notes on color, composition, and the painting's label. Your paper will compare that painting with one of the works we've discussed in class.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the museum visit?
options: To gather material for a comparison paper
To attend a lecture by a museum curator
To photograph paintings for a class display
To choose a topic for a group presentation
questions.explanation: Students must study one painting and compare it with a work discussed in class for their paper.

questions.prompt: What does the professor say about taking pictures in the museum?
options: Students may take pictures without using flash.
Students need special permission to take pictures.
Pictures are allowed only in the landscape gallery.
Pictures may be taken only on weekday mornings.
questions.explanation: He says photography is allowed but flash is not.

If neither time works for you, send me an email and we can set up a short video call instead.

The math building is closed on Tuesdays.

questions.prompt: What can students do if they cannot attend the new office hours?
options: Arrange a video call by email
Go to the tutoring center on Wednesdays
Post questions on the course website
Visit the professor's office instead

intro: Listen to an announcement at the campus library.
text: Attention, library visitors. Starting Monday and continuing through the end of final exams, the main library will stay open twenty-four hours a day. After midnight, you'll need to show your student ID at the front entrance to come in. The café on the ground floor will also stay open until two a.m. Please remember that the third floor is a silent study area at all hours, so take phone calls and group discussions to the first floor.

questions.prompt: What change is the librarian announcing?
options: The library will close early during finals.
The library will be open all night during finals.
A new study area will open on the third floor.
The café will move to the first floor.
questions.explanation: He says the main library will stay open twenty-four hours a day through final exams.

questions.prompt: What must visitors do to enter the library after midnight?
options: Reserve a study room online
Show a student ID at the entrance
Enter through the ground-floor café
Sign a list at the circulation desk

intro: Listen to an announcement on the campus radio station.
text: Good morning. This is a message from Campus Transportation. Because of road construction on College Avenue, the blue shuttle line will follow a detour for the next three weeks. Buses will not stop at the Student Union. Instead, please use the temporary stop on Elm Street, about a block away. Expect delays of five to ten minutes during busy hours. Updated maps are available on the transportation website.

questions.prompt: Why is the shuttle route changing?
options: Construction is taking place on a nearby road.
The Student Union is being renovated.
Fewer students are riding the blue line.
The shuttle company has hired new drivers.
questions.explanation: The detour is caused by road construction on College Avenue.

At a temporary stop on Elm Street
At the next stop on College Avenue
Inside the Student Union lobby

intro: Listen to an announcement at a new student orientation.
text: Welcome, everyone! I'm one of your orientation leaders. Here's the plan for the rest of today. At one o'clock, we'll split into small groups for a campus tour, so check your name tag for your group color. At three, you'll meet with an academic advisor to choose your first-semester classes. Then at six, there's a free dinner on the main lawn. If it rains, dinner moves to the gym.

options: By the major they have chosen
By the advisor they are meeting
By the color on their name tag
By the dorm they will live in

Students will take a campus tour.
Students will have dinner on the lawn.
Students will go to the gym for games.
questions.explanation: At three, students meet an advisor to choose their first-semester classes.

Lap swim classes are canceled for the week, but the instructors will hold dry-land training sessions in Studio B at the usual times.

Its filtration system is being replaced.
Its lap lanes are being repainted.

They will be moved to different times.
They will be extended by an extra week.
They will be replaced by training in a studio.

intro: Listen to an announcement at a campus basketball game.
text: Good evening, fans, and thanks for coming out to tonight's game! A few quick notes. At halftime, we'll hold a free-throw contest, and three students chosen from the crowd will compete for a semester parking pass. Also, the first five hundred students through the gates received a free team T-shirt. If you got one, wear it to Saturday's home game, when we're trying to fill the arena with our school color.

options: A free team T-shirt
Tickets to Saturday's home game
A parking pass for the semester
A meal at the campus café

Take part in the halftime contest
Give the shirts to other students
Bring the shirts to be signed by players

text: Good afternoon, everyone. It's my pleasure to announce the winners of this year's student poetry contest. We received over two hundred entries, the most in the contest's history. First place goes to Daniel Reyes, a sophomore in biology, for his poem about his grandmother's garden. It received more entries than ever before.

It was judged by students instead of faculty.

options: It will be read aloud at graduation.
It will be displayed in a campus garden.
It will be entered in a national contest.
It will appear in a campus magazine.

intro: Listen to an announcement in a physics class.
text: Before you leave, there's been a change to the final exam that'll affect how you study. Originally, I said the final would only cover material since the midterm. However, after reviewing your midterm results, I've decided to make it cumulative, since several early concepts, especially conservation of momentum, clearly need reinforcement. To balance that out, you'll be allowed to bring one page of handwritten formulas. Printed or photocopied sheets won't be accepted, so start compiling yours now.

questions.prompt: Why did the professor decide to make the final exam cumulative?
options: Students requested a single comprehensive review.
The department requires all finals to be cumulative.
The material since the midterm was too limited.
Midterm results showed weaknesses in earlier material.
questions.explanation: He says the midterm results showed that early concepts like momentum need reinforcement.

questions.prompt: Why does the professor allow students to bring a formula sheet?
options: To offset the exam's broader coverage
To reward students who did well on the midterm
To replace the formulas printed in the textbook
To reduce the number of questions on the exam
questions.explanation: He presents the handwritten formula sheet as a way to balance out the more demanding cumulative exam.

intro: Listen to an announcement in an anthropology class.
text: A reminder about your fieldwork projects. Anyone planning to interview people, even friends or family, must collect a signed consent form from each participant before the interview takes place, not afterward. Forms collected after the fact won't count, and I won't be able to accept data gathered without them. Also, remove names and any identifying details from your transcripts. If your project only involves observing public spaces, you don't need consent forms, but please describe your observation site in your proposal.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To describe how to choose a public observation site
To announce a new deadline for project proposals
To explain the rules for collecting data from participants
To discourage students from interviewing family members
questions.explanation: The professor outlines consent and privacy requirements for gathering fieldwork data.

questions.prompt: What does the professor imply about interview data gathered before consent is obtained?
options: It must be stored separately from other data.
It is acceptable if participants are relatives.
It can be used if all names are removed.
It cannot be used in the project.
questions.explanation: Since forms collected afterward do not count and she cannot accept data gathered without them, such data is unusable.

intro: Listen to an announcement in a microbiology lab.
text: Everyone, please listen carefully before handling today's cultures. Although the bacteria we're using aren't considered dangerous, we treat every sample as potentially infectious. That means gloves and lab coats stay on until you've disinfected your bench. Broken glass that has touched a culture doesn't go in the regular glass box; it goes in the red sharps container by the sink. And if you spill anything, don't wipe it up immediately. Cover it with paper towels, soak it with disinfectant, and wait ten minutes.

questions.prompt: Why does the lab coordinator mention that the bacteria are not considered dangerous?
options: To reassure students that gloves are unnecessary
To stress that precautions are required regardless
To explain why spills can be cleaned up quickly
To show that the experiment has been simplified
questions.explanation: He contrasts their low risk with the rule that every sample is treated as potentially infectious.

questions.prompt: What should students do first if they spill a culture?
options: Cover the spill with paper towels
Wipe it up with disinfectant right away
Report it to the lab coordinator
Place it in the red sharps container
questions.explanation: He says not to wipe it up but to cover it with paper towels, then soak it with disinfectant.

intro: Listen to an announcement in an environmental science class.
text: About next Friday's trip to the Pine Hollow wetlands: you'll need to submit the signed liability waiver by Wednesday, or you won't be able to board the van. Bring waterproof boots. The boardwalk is partly flooded this season, and we'll be wading in to collect water samples. If heavy rain is forecast, we'll postpone to the following Friday rather than cancel, so keep that date open. Anyone who can't attend either day should see me about an alternative assignment.

questions.prompt: What will happen if heavy rain is forecast for the day of the trip?
options: The trip will be canceled entirely.
Students will collect samples from the boardwalk only.
The trip will be moved to the following week.
All students will complete an alternative assignment.
questions.explanation: She says the trip would be postponed to the following Friday rather than canceled.

questions.prompt: Why does the professor tell students to bring waterproof boots?
options: Heavy rain is expected on Friday.
The van will park far from the boardwalk.
The waiver requires protective footwear.
They will walk through water to take samples.
questions.explanation: She explains that they will be wading in to collect water samples.

intro: Listen to an announcement in an architecture class.
text: I'm delighted to confirm that Maria Lindqvist, the structural engineer behind the new pedestrian bridge downtown, will join us on Thursday. Since her talk focuses on the bridge's cable design, I'd strongly suggest reviewing chapter seven on tension structures beforehand; otherwise, much of it may be hard to follow. Because she's speaking during our regular session, attendance counts as usual. Afterward, she's agreed to stay for informal questions, so if you're considering a career in engineering, that's a rare opportunity.

It will focus mainly on chapter seven.
It may be especially valuable for some students.
It will take place on a different day.

intro: Listen to an announcement in a linguistics class.
text: Let me clarify the policy on term paper drafts, since there's been some confusion. Submitting a draft is optional, but if you turn one in by November fifteenth, I'll give you written feedback, and you'll be allowed to revise the final version after it's graded. Students who skip the draft won't have that revision option. As for late final papers, they'll lose five percent per day, with no exceptions except documented emergencies.

questions.prompt: What is the professor mainly doing?
options: Explaining how to give feedback on drafts
Announcing a change in the paper's topic
Extending the deadline for final papers
Clarifying the rules for submitting term papers

options: They avoid penalties for late final papers.
They may revise their paper after grading.
They receive five extra percentage points.
They can choose a later final deadline.

intro: Listen to an announcement on the campus radio station.
text: As many of you know, renovation of the library's east wing begins next month. During construction, the print journals and newspapers housed there will be moved temporarily to the Science Annex. Most current journals will remain available, but older volumes will be placed in off-site storage. You can still request them online, and they'll be delivered to the main circulation desk within two business days. We expect the east wing to reopen by the start of fall semester.

options: Why the library decided to renovate the east wing
A new online system for borrowing library books
How a renovation will affect access to library materials
The opening of a new science library on campus

options: They will be kept in the Science Annex.
Patrons will not be able to get them immediately.
They will no longer be available to students.
They can be viewed only in digital form.
questions.explanation: Because they must be requested and take up to two business days to arrive, access is delayed.

intro: Listen to an announcement at a student government meeting.
text: Good afternoon. Beginning in January, the university will launch a bike-share program with stations at ten locations across campus. Students can ride free for the first thirty minutes of each trip. At the same time, the price of daytime parking permits will rise by fifteen percent. The additional revenue won't go into the general budget; instead, it will fund the bike-share system and expanded shuttle service. Our goal is to give commuters practical alternatives, not just higher fees.

questions.prompt: What will the money from higher parking fees be used for?
options: Supporting alternative ways to travel on campus
Building additional parking areas on campus
Repairing the roads around the university
Adding to the university's general budget
questions.explanation: He says the revenue will fund the bike-share system and expanded shuttle service.

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker mention that the extra revenue will not go into the general budget?
options: To explain why the bike-share program is free
To suggest that the budget has been reduced
To apologize for the higher cost of permits
To show that the fee increase serves a specific purpose
questions.explanation: He emphasizes that the money is earmarked for transportation alternatives.

intro: Listen to an announcement at a graduate research symposium.
text: Thank you all for attending this year's symposium. Before we close, I'm pleased to announce the winner of the Graduate Research Prize. options: It was completed faster than the other projects.
It was the only engineering project entered.
It had already been adopted by several cities.
It could help cities with little money for repairs.
questions.explanation: The judges noted its potential to help cities with limited maintenance budgets.
